title: Jetavanaramaya
summary: The Jetavanaramaya is a stupa at Jetavana in Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka, begun by King Mahasena, whose reign one page gives as 273 to 301 CE, and finished by his son. Guinness World Records gives a base area of 233,000 m2 and a height of 70.4 m today, 122 m with its lost original spire. A 12th-century restoration under Parakramabahu I lowered it.

uncertainty.note: Start is the beginning of Mahasena's reign as given by Ceylon History (273 to 301); Amazing Lanka gives 276 to 303; Guinness says 'When completed in 301'. End is the present: the stupa stands.

phases.description: Begun by King Mahasena (reign 273-301 per Ceylon History) and completed by his son; Guinness says "When completed in 301". Amazing Lanka gives Mahasena as 276-303.
Stands at its full original height until the 12th-century restoration; the pages opened record no earlier alteration.

In the 12th century King Parakramabahu I began restoration, which lowered the stupa from its original height to about 71 m (Amazing Lanka); 70.4 m per Guinness. Year is the start of the 12th century; the pages give no exact year.

reviewer_note: Shape stupa. Least sure of: (1) all three publishers are non-institutional (Guinness classed reference); no government, museum or university page opened, and the Sunday Observer, CNN and Lakpura pages were blocked. (2) No diameter on any opened page: the platform side of 177 m is used as the plan size; the circumference of 366 m (Amazing Lanka) is not used. (3) The 12th-century phase start 1101 is a placeholder for "12th century". (4) Reign dates differ: 273-301 vs 276-303.
